findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: There was a foam cup being used as a scoop to handle salsa. The scoop lacks a handle and the outer surfaces were observed in direct contact with the food item. Discussed with the PIC and the cup was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that scoops contain handles and are stored in a manner that protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a container of cooked shrimp stored inside of a line cooler that lacked date marking. The PIC added a date marking to the shrimps to correct the violation. Ensure that all cooked foods are date marked with the date that it is prepared.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed an employee repeatedly tap knife on the surface of the trash can in the midst of prepping avocados. The practice was ceased and corrected on site. The kitchen manager discussed proper food handling with the employee and the knife was sanitized during the visit. Ensure that clean food contact surfaces are sanitized whenever cross contamination occurs.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility is in full operation and no sanitizer buckets were available. Discussed with the person-in-charge and two sanitizer buckets were prepared and tested at 200ppm (quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are available at all times if food prep is occurring.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(A) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: There were ground beef patties stored above seafood in the standing cooler along the cook-line. Shown to PIC and the containers were rearranged. Discussed that ground beef has a higher cooking temperature than seafood, therefore, ground beef must always be stored beneath seafood. Ensure that ground beef is never stored above seafood to protect against contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.comment: The facility could not locate any signed employee health forms. Blank forms were provided to the facility for employees to complete. The forms were signed to correct the violation. Ensure that health forms are available and accessible for future routine inspections.
findings.citation_text: 2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: A personal drink was observed stored on top of the dish machine. Discussed with PIC the potential for cross contamination of clean dishes. Ensure that personal drinks are never stored in manner that can contaminate food items, single service items, or food contact surfaces. The drink was removed to correct the violation.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: An employee moved a trash can with gloved hands and then proceeded to handling food without switching gloves. The activity was ceased and corrected. Ensure that single service gloves are limited to one task and if tasks are interrupted, be sure to remove gloves, wash hands, and don new gloves.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.15(A) Gloves, Use Limitation. (A) If used, single-use gloves shall be used for only one task such as working with ready-to-eat food or with raw animal food, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The soda gun in the bar area was observed soiled with dried liquids. Discussed and shown to PIC. The soda gun was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that food contact surfaces are cleaned as frequent as necessary to prevent build up.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: A pan of gravy stored on the stovetop was observed at room temperature. PIC mentioned that the facility planned to reheat the gravy later in the day. Discussed with PIC that TCS (temperature/time control) foods must be either cold held or hot held to ensure safety of food items. PIC mentioned that he got distracted and that the gravy was mistakenly left at room temperature from the early morning. The gravy was discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that foods that are hot held are maintained at 135F or above and never held at room temperature.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: A large container of cooked chicken broth was observed actively cooling at room temperature (with lid on container). Discussed with PIC proper methods for cooling TCS foods. A cooling handout was given to the facility as reference. The broth was portioned into shallow pans to allow for the broth to cool quickly and efficiently. If using the shallow pan method for cooling, ensure that TCS foods are placed in smaller portions and in shallow pans to allow for the item to cool within the proper timeframe for safety.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.15(A) Cooling Methods. (A) Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria specified under § 3-501.14 by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of FOOD being cooled: (1) Placing the food in shallow pans; (2) Separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; (3) Using rapid cooling equipment; (4) Stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; (5) Using containers that facilitate heat transfer; (6) Adding ice as an ingredient; or (7) Other effective methods.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The standing Pepsi cooler in the service area was observed with an ambient temperature of 50F. A container of cream cheese was probed at 46F. The facility adjusted the temperature knob to a higher number that is sufficient enough for properly cold hold. The temperature of the cooler was observed at 41F after adjusting the temperature knob. Be sure that cold holding equipment is maintained at 41F or below in order to ensure proper cold holding temperatures for TCS foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Portions of cooked rice were observed in the walk in cooler in plastic bags. Discussed and shown to PIC. The bags of rice were discarded. Ensure that foods are never stored in plastic bags, as it is not an approved food contact surface, nor is it durable and sufficient enough to withstand repeated ware-washing.  

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Items such as but not limited to test strips, a sani bucket, and plates were being stored on the cutting boards along the cook-line of the kitchen. Discussed proper storage of items with PIC to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces and Ready-to-Eat food items that are placed on the boards. The cutting boards were sanitized by the PIC. Ensure that food contact surfaces are never exposed to contamination.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed several containers of raw chicken stored above containers of cheeses in the walk in cooler. Discussed with PIC the proper storage order for food items. Ensure that poultry is never stored above ready-to-eat food to prevent contamination. Cheese should always be stored above raw poultry. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the sani bucket in the serving station to be 0ppm (CL). PIC noted that sani buckets are normally changed at 2pm and that staff hadn’t gotten to them yet. The sani buckets were changed and tested again at 100ppm (CL). Ensure that sani buckets are maintained at the recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize surfaces. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
A gallon of whole milk was probed at 53F in a Pepsi cooler located in the kitchen area. PIC noted that the milk was stored in the cooler overnight. The milk was discarded and the knob inside of the cooler was adjusted to lower the temperature of the unit. Ensure that milk is always held at a temperature of 41F or less. 

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Observed a container of almond milk to be stored with various drinks intended for public consumption. PIC noted that the almond milk was for personal use. The milk container was removed from the cooler. Ensure that personal food and drink items are stored separate from items that will be served to the public to prevent contamination.  

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  

At the beginning of the inspection, there weren’t any employee health reporting forms on file for employees. Discussed with Manager that all employees must report to PIC if sick. Inspector provided employee health agreement forms for employees to sign. Employee health agreements have all been signed and will be stored in binder. Ensure that all new employees sign and complete employee health agreement forms when hired.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

At least two employees were observed turning off faucet handles using barehand contact during the hand-washing process. Discussed with PIC that employees must use a barrier when turning off the faucet to prevent recontaminating hands. Ensure that employees always use a barrier when turning off faucet handles after washing hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The ice machine was observed to have mold on a pipe located at the back inside of the machine. Discussed with the PIC that the inside of the ice machine should be cleaned as needed to prevent mold buildup. The ice machine has been cleaned and corrected. Ensure that the ice machine is cleaned regularly and free of mold buildup.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

Two sanitizer buckets were observed to have a 0ppm CL concentration. PIC noted that the facility uses Chorine as a sanitizer. Both sani buckets were changed and tested again to have a 100ppm concentration. Ensure that sani buckets are always maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

The dish washing machine was observed to have a concentration of 0ppm CL when tested. Discussed with PIC and EcoLab was contacted to come service the dish machine. The service tech is expected to come later today or tomorrow to service the dish machine. The facility was instructed to use the three compartment sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. Ensure that the sanitizing concentration for the dish machine is maintained at the manufacturer’s recommendation in order to properly sanitize.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

There was a pan of salsa and a pan of beans stored in the walk-in cooler that was dated 1/16/2024. These TCS foods exceeded the 7-day time criteria for cold holding. Discussed with PIC that both the beans and the salsa was out of date and both items were discarded. Ensure that all TCS foods don’t exceed the 7-day time criteria for cold holding.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Two mop buckets were observed to have mop heads placed inside of the bucket in waste water. Discussed with PIC that mop heads must be placed in a position that allows for them to dry properly. Mop heads were removed from waste water and stored in a position to air dry. Waste water was also dumped. Ensure that mop heads are always placed in a position for them to air dry after each use.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

(REPEAT) The wait station cabinet doors and interior were observed to have soda splatter. Discussed with PIC to clean the inside of the cabinet area as needed. Ensure that the wait station interior cabinets are free of splatter and cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

(REPEAT) Certified Food Protection Managers have not completed allergen training. Provide allergen training for all CFPMs.
